classification.habit: Erect perennial undershrub, 30–90 cm tall, with milky latex.
classification.habitat: Moist, shady tropical forests and forest margins, often under the canopy in humus-rich soil.
classification.distribution: Sub-Himalayan tract from Punjab to Assam, the Western and Eastern Ghats and the Andamans; now largely cultivated as wild stocks are depleted.

identification.description: Tapering tortuous cylindrical roots with pale greyish-brown corky bark bearing longitudinal fissures, bitter persistent taste, odorless.
identification.whole_plant: Glabrous erect undershrub with whorled leaves, terminal clusters of small pinkish-white flowers and shiny purple-black drupes.
identification.root: Tuberous, tortuous, sub-cylindrical roots 8–15 cm long and 0.5–2 cm thick; outer surface greyish-yellow to brown with irregular longitudinal fissures; fracture short; slight odour and bitter taste.
identification.stem: Erect, pale, sparsely branched stem with milky latex and conspicuous leaf scars.
identification.leaf: Leaves in whorls of 3–4, elliptic-lanceolate to obovate, 7–18 cm long, acute, bright green above and pale beneath.
identification.flower: Small tubular flowers in long-stalked terminal or axillary corymbose cymes; corolla white with a pink to red tube, calyx and pedicels bright red.
identification.fruit: Small drupes, single or didymous (paired), turning shining purplish-black when ripe.
identification.seed: One ovoid, wrinkled seed in each drupe.
identification_points: Tapering tortuous cylindrical roots with pale greyish-brown corky bark bearing longitudinal fissures, bitter persistent taste, odorless.

therapeutics.precautions: Potent drug with strong central and cardiovascular depressant action; use the root only under qualified supervision and in the API dose (1–2 g churna). Avoid self-medication and long unsupervised use; may cause nasal congestion, drowsiness, bradycardia and low mood. Not to be combined with conventional antihypertensives or sedatives without medical advice.
therapeutics.contraindications: Pregnancy and lactation; depression or history of suicidal ideation; peptic ulcer and ulcerative colitis; hypotension, bradycardia; patients on MAO inhibitors, digoxin or other antihypertensives without supervision.

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: The root contains indole alkaloids (about 1–2% total), of which reserpine is the best known; it depletes catecholamine stores, explaining the sedative and blood-pressure-lowering effects.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Indian snakeroot is a powerful herb for managing high blood pressure and calming anxiety, but should be used with caution.
recognized_uses: Source of reserpine and ajmaline in conventional pharmacology
Traditional use in Anidra, Unmada and raised blood pressure
modern_information.safety_notes: Reserpine-containing material can cause depression, nasal stuffiness, bradycardia, hypotension and gastric hyperacidity; dosing should stay within API limits and under medical supervision.

Irregular longitudinal fissures on the root surface

student.quick_revision: Sarpagandha (Rauvolfia serpentina): root; Tikta-Katu rasa, Ruksha-Laghu guna, Ushna virya, Katu vipaka; Kapha-Vata shamaka; Nidrajanana, Raktavata-shamaka; used in Anidra, Unmada and high blood pressure, with caution.

teaching_points: Link the alkaloid reserpine to the classical Nidraprada and Hridayavasadaka karma.
Stress the conservation status: wild Sarpagandha is threatened and cultivated root is preferred.
Explain why the drug is used under supervision and in small doses.
discussion_points: Reserpine and the modern history of Sarpagandha in hypertension
Nidrajanana action versus safety limits (depression, hypotension)
practical_points: Examine root pieces for fissured greyish-brown surface, short fracture and bitter taste.
Show herbarium specimens with whorled leaves, red pedicels and paired drupes.

doctor.quick_reference: Sarpagandha root (Tikta-Katu, Ushna) is used as Nidraprada and in Unmada and raised blood pressure; potent reserpine-containing drug, 1–2 g churna under supervision.
key_precautions: Watch for hypotension, bradycardia and nasal congestion
Do not combine with antihypertensives or sedatives without supervision
